findings.title: Gift before distinction
findings.claim: 17:20 says provision reaches both orientations and is not withheld; beside it, the focus's physical carriage is received support and Noah's gratitude is a response to that support, not proof that aid is offered only to his line.
findings.mechanism: The focus supplies physical carriage and grateful recognition. 17:20 names provision extended to both groups and an unblocked gift; 17:21 then distinguishes degrees. Their contact changes carriage from a unique mark of access into one received gift within a broader pattern of shared provision and differentiated outcomes.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can distinguish receiving aid from the way a recipient responds to it.
findings.containment: 17:20 may concern worldly provision too remote to qualify the ark rescue directly; the focus still names a particular company carried with Noah. The reading does not erase later differences of degree or equate all recipients' outcomes.

epistemic.reason: The focus and 17:20 HFT anchors are complete, and 17:21 is separately present in the packet. The comparison between common provision and the particular rescue remains an attributed contextual inference.

findings.mechanism: The supplied ع ب د branch occurs in the focus and in 17:5's sent servants, who belong to God and are described as severe. Noah's separate gratitude predicate differentiates his praised mode within a servant relation that can also describe commanded agents.
findings.reader_payoff: The modifier شَكُورًا carries Noah's evaluative distinction; the noun عَبْدًا alone does not supply the whole praise.
findings.containment: The focus and 17:5 do not equate Noah's moral standing with the sent agents. The connection record calls their uses unrelated, so purposeful contrast remains an alternative; the shared relation and separate modifier support only the bounded distinction stated here.
